rationale: A wins because it keeps the cleanest rollout story: "AI tutoring is about to reach a million more public-school students — through 30 districts at once" is a real K-12 adoption angle with scale, timing, and proof needs. B is sharp, but it burns a slot on "What one pilot district saw when students used an AI tutor regularly" before it has a named district, teacher, parent, or district-level result. That is not fatal, but it is the difference between a set a founder can use now and one that needs a proof hunt before it stops wobbling.
gaps_in_A: "Donors, not school districts, are footing the bill" overstates the supplied fact. The update says Khanmigo is free to teachers and donor-funded; it does not prove districts pay nothing.
"Khan Academy answers the independent-thinking critics directly" assumes Khan has an answer on record. The proof section correctly asks for that, but the headline gets ahead of the facts.
"30 districts signing on simultaneously" is a touch too tidy. The update says rolling out to 30 more districts, not that all signed at once or through the same mechanism.
gaps_in_B: "What one pilot district saw when students used an AI tutor regularly" is a conditional local angle presented as a kept angle. No district, teacher, student, or district-level result is in the update.
"Khanmigo reaches 1 million students" is refused as "no_journalist_shape," but A shows the missing shape: district AI adoption at 30-district scale. B throws away a usable scale story.
"Donors, not districts, are paying" repeats the same overclaim it later questions. "Free to teachers" is not the same as free to districts or students.

"Until those two proofs exist, every angle above is a shape with a hole" is too blunt. The funding angle needs donor and cost proof; the critic angle needs educator and product-response proof, not necessarily the study methodology and a named district.
